recommendation.recommendation: Implement immediate supplemental irrigation and apply organic soil amendments to relieve severe water stress and increase soil organic carbon.
recommendation.justification: Satellite data show critical water stress (NDWI -0.20) and canopy loss (NDVI 0.15). Weather forecasts indicate below‑optimal rainfall, while soil tests confirm optimal pH, high nitrogen, but low organic carbon. Immediate irrigation will restore moisture for the flowering stage, and organic amendments will improve soil structure, reduce erosion risk, and support disease resistance, allowing the farmer to capture strong market prices.
actions: Apply flood irrigation today to deliver at least 30 mm of water across the field; repeat every 7‑10 days until rainfall meets crop demand.
If flood irrigation is not feasible, install temporary drip lines and schedule 5‑6 L m⁻² per day for the next two weeks.
Incorporate 5‑7 t ha⁻¹ of well‑composted organic manure or compost into the top 15 cm of soil within the next 7 days.
Conduct a quick visual scout for Fusarium or Verticillium wilt symptoms and aphid/bollworm presence; treat with recommended fungicides/insecticides if detected.
Record field moisture readings (tensiometer or soil moisture probe) at 20 cm depth after each irrigation event.
recommendation.expected_outcome: Restored soil moisture will halt canopy decline, improve NDVI to >0.4 within 2 weeks, reduce disease risk, and position the crop for a normal yield, enabling sale at the current high market price of ~7,600 INR/quintal.
monitoring_plan: Daily visual check of plant vigor and wilting signs.
Weekly NDVI/NDWI satellite image review (or drone NDVI if available).
Soil moisture measurement twice per week at multiple field points.
Record irrigation volumes and dates in a logbook.
Bi‑weekly soil test for organic carbon to track amendment effectiveness.

actions: Apply flood irrigation today to deliver at least 30 mm of water across the field; repeat every 7‑10 days until rainfall meets crop demand.
If flood irrigation is not feasible, install temporary drip lines and schedule 5‑6 L m⁻² per day for the next two weeks.
Incorporate 5‑7 t ha⁻¹ of well‑composted organic manure or compost into the top 15 cm of soil within the next 7 days.
Conduct a quick visual scout for Fusarium or Verticillium wilt symptoms and aphid/bollworm presence; treat with recommended fungicides/insecticides if detected.
Record field moisture readings (tensiometer or soil moisture probe) at 20 cm depth after each irrigation event.

Weather forecasts indicate below‑optimal rainfall, while soil tests confirm optimal pH, high nitrogen, but low organic carbon. Immediate irrigation will restore moisture for the flowering stage, and organic amendments will improve soil structure, reduce erosion risk, and support disease resistance, allowing the farmer to capture strong market prices.
